title: Minimal Pairs — Clarity↔opacity; Reflection↔refraction
content_html:
Minimal Pairs — clarity↔opacity; reflection↔refraction

English ⇄ Cantonese (繁體) with Jyutping and literal glosses

clarity ↔ opacity (antonymic pair)

English Cantonese Jyutping Literal gloss Core meaning
clarity 清晰 cing1 sik1 clear • distinct quality of being easy to see or understand
opacity 不透明 bat1 tau3 ming4 not • pass • light quality of not letting light/information through; obscurity

Usage cues

  • Clarity: optics (image clarity), writing (clarity of argument).
  • Opacity: materials (paint opacity), prose (legal opacity).

Contrast tests

“Increase the window’s __ for privacy.” → opacity
“We edited the report for __.” → clarity

Common collocations

  • high/visual/semantic clarity
  • increase/reduce opacity; opacity setting (graphics)

Mnemonic

Cantonese mirrors meaning: 清(“clear”) + 晰(“distinct”). 不透明 literally “not‑pass‑light.”

reflection (optics) ↔ refraction (near‑confusables)

English Cantonese Jyutping Literal gloss Core meaning
reflection (optics) 反射 faan2 se6 turn‑back • emit light (or sound) bounces off a surface; angle in = angle out
refraction 折射 zit3 se6 bend/break • emit light bends as it passes between media of different refractive index

Diagnostic frames

Mirror → reflection (光線被反射)

Air → water → bent straw → refraction (光線被折射)

Formula cues

  • Reflection: θᵢ = θᵣ
  • Refraction (Snell’s law): n₁·sinθ₁ = n₂·sinθ₂

Contrast tests

“A calm lake acts like a mirror due to __.” → reflection
“A straw looks bent in water due to __.” → refraction

Avoid this ambiguity

reflection can also mean “introspection” (反思 faan2 si1). For the optical pair here, use 反射.

Mnemonic

reFLECtion → think “flex back” (bounce); reFRACtion → think “fracture path” (bend).
